solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finger problem exhibited by party pooper

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the words party pooper, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A spoilsport at a celebration has some trouble with a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger problem' suggests an injury, but it means a mistake made while typing.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the typing finger produces a misprint, so a finger problem is a keyboard error.

clue.text: Also spotted singer keeping book cleaner

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: the bird holds the book's letter inside itself

parts.note: the song thrush has a speckled breast and a fine song

explanation.surface: A speckled songbird is also hanging on to a book that a cleaner has.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothbrush is a tool for cleaning teeth.

clue.text: Union rules schools introducing new uniform

indicators.note: the schools take the new and uniform letters in among their own

parts.note: preps are preparatory schools
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trade union's regulations require schools to bring in fresh dress codes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenuptial agreements set terms for a marriage, so they are rules governing a union.

clue.text: Fail to criticise a suggestion about power

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for criticising them

indicators.note: the pieces a and suggestion go around the letter for power, so it sits inside them

parts.note: a point is a suggestion put forward
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone declines to find fault with a proposal about energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside A POINT, giving APPOINT.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappoint someone is to fail them, falling short of what they hoped for.

clue.text: Having no base in Paris he meets soldier in pub

parts.note: il is French for he

indicators.note: the soldier goes within the pub

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A Frenchman meets a soldier in a bar, with no home base.
explanation.definitionFit: An illogical argument is unfounded, with nothing sound to rest on.

clue.text: Stockpile a lot of documents head of army sent in

indicators.note: the letter is dispatched into the middle of the documents

parts.note: MSS abbreviates manuscripts, several documents

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of army

explanation.surface: A stack of files is stored after the army chief submits them.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather a large quantity, building up a hoard.

clue.text: Frank often replaces these collector's items

definitions.text: Frank often replaces these collector's items

parts.words: Frank often replaces these collector's items
parts.note: frank is a postal verb: a franking machine marks mail paid, doing away with the sticky labels philatelists collect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the post office verb for marking a letter as paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Franked mail carries a printed mark in place of the adhesive labels that philatelists collect.

clue.text: Someone in acre with capital?

parts.note: with a capital letter acre becomes Acre, a port city in the Middle East whose residents share that nationality

explanation.walkthrough: 'acre' looks like a land measure; capitalise it and it is the city in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient port in northern Israel, so a resident there is a national of that country.

clue.text: Flap over Dorothy lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the name raises it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A commotion about a woman being picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, which is what a flap is.

clue.text: Completed a couple of lines on average

parts.note: something over is finished or completed
L is an abbreviation for line, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: Someone finished a pair of verses that were merely middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall describes the general picture taken as a whole, much like on average.

clue.text: A milkman doing trips for beasts in general

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so the letters of a milkman doing fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A milkman on his rounds keeps falling over on behalf of the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal kingdom is the whole category of living fauna, all creatures taken together.

clue.text: Confident when taken to court about source of revenue

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the word for taken to court goes around the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: someone sued has been taken to court

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter, here the first of revenue

explanation.surface: A tax authority feels sure of itself when prosecuted over income.
explanation.definitionFit: An assured person is self-possessed and certain, which is being confident.

clue.text: Living area accommodating French art gallery

parts.note: housing people is accommodating them
art is the old second-person form of 'are', and French for 'thou art' is 'tu es'
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A residential district is home to a French art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' looks like painting, but 'art' is the verb (thou art), French 'es'. In Britain a housing estate is a planned development of homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a planned district of homes, a residential area.

clue.text: Miss school drama article placed for son in trust

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: the article is put where the son's letter was, replacing it

parts.note: S is the genealogy abbreviation for son
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A school play's script puts an object where a boy had been in a charitable fund.
explanation.definitionFit: To play truant is to stay away from lessons without permission.

clue.text: Emperor backs a follower of another one

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the word for emperor is read in reverse

parts.note: a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: One emperor supports a disciple of a rival monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another one' points back to 'Emperor': the answer's faith follows Haile Selassie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia, so one is a follower of a different emperor.

clue.text: A nice long novel can be relaxing

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of a nice long are made new in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pleasant, lengthy book can be a calming read.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial company or surroundings are pleasant and agreeable, which makes them relaxing.

clue.text: Original shots, say, drunk by locals

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is swallowed up inside the locals

parts.note: natives are local people
eg (for example) is the abbreviation meaning say

explanation.surface: First rounds of drinks are knocked back by the regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' and 'drunk' suggest drinks; the shots are photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic negatives are the first images from which prints are made.

clue.text: Stimulate boxer to eat large starter

parts.note: to spark something is to stimulate or set it off

indicators.note: the dog takes the letter for large inside itself as if swallowing it

parts.note: a pug is a slang word for a boxer, short for pugilist
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone motivates a fighter to have a big breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a dog breed, but here it is the fighter, PUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A spark plug ignites the fuel in an engine, so it gets the motor going: a starter.

clue.text: Frugal, like soccer team having had to spend pounds

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: spending the pounds means they are gone, so the letter for pounds is removed

parts.note: Celtic is a Glasgow football club
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A football club forced to part with its cash becomes thrifty.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic lives austerely, denying themselves comforts, which is frugal living.

clue.text: Reserves place for supplier of ham that's appetising

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a sty is where pigs, which supply ham, are kept

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside room for a pork producer whose goods look delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty food is full of flavour and appetising.

clue.text: Observed transporting nine tons in square

indicators.note: the word for observed carries the other letters within it

parts.note: seen means observed
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone was spotted carrying nine tons into a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a town square, but it is a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is four times four, a perfect square.

clue.text: Real sociable type's a help for builder

parts.note: concrete means real and tangible
a good mixer is someone who socialises easily

explanation.surface: A genuinely outgoing person is a boon to a builder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cement mixer prepares the mortar and concrete builders need, so it is a useful aid on site.

clue.text: One who regrets imprisoning Liberal head of state?

indicators.note: the one who regrets holds the letter for Liberal locked inside

parts.note: a ruer is one who rues, regretting

explanation.surface: A repentant figure has jailed a Liberal leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state?' is a definition by example, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch or president, who governs and heads a country, is one example; the question mark flags this.

clue.text: Dispatched two varieties of diamonds

parts.note: the first of the two kinds of diamonds is ice, slang for diamond jewellery
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds, the second kind

explanation.surface: A jeweller sent off a pair of different kinds of diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two varieties of diamonds' gives the word diamonds two meanings, once as jewel slang and once as the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is slang for killing them, and dispatched means killed.

clue.text: Fortress initially constructed with ornate detail

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of constructed
ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of detail are fancifully rearranged

explanation.surface: A stronghold was built with elaborate decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortified stronghold, often guarding a city.

clue.text: Running races after rocket: that's guts!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the rocket

parts.note: the V-1 was a German wartime flying bomb, written V1 and read as VI

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters of races are rearranged

explanation.surface: Racing straight after a rocket launch takes real nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage but means innards. 'Running' turns RACES into SCERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, the innards or guts.

clue.text: Take weight off Green politician in bandage

indicators.note: the green and politician pieces go inside the word for bandage

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it
eco- is a prefix meaning environmental, green
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An environmentalist MP wrapped in dressings should lose some pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take weight off' sounds like dieting, but it means relieving pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompress something is to release the pressure on it, relieving the load.

clue.text: Turning, smack annoying flier

indicators.note: turning means turning round, so the word for smack is written backwards

parts.note: a smack of something is a taste or flavour, a tang

explanation.surface: Someone spins and swats an irritating insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a tiny biting insect, a pest that flies around people.
